Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the EcoNova Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone and wait for further instructions. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EcoNova Renewables' results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Development Officer; and Lena Novak, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. EcoNova Renewables had a strong third quarter, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

This quarter's achievements stand out across five crucial areas that underscore our momentum. First, the substantial impact of government incentives and subsidies, which have become foundational to our scaling efforts. Second, the securing of significant new power purchase agreements with compelling average pricing. Third, robust progress on construction fronts and firm commercial operation dates. Fourth, standout overall performance highlights and key milestones. And fifth, meaningful growth in our operating capacity and generation output. These elements collectively drive our leadership in clean tech.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with our financial results for the third quarter. Revenue reached $1.8 billion, representing a 24% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 20.1%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $500 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Adjusted EBITDA hit $285 million, up 62% year-over-year. Net income was $285 million, or $0.87 per diluted share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Let me expand on some of these drivers, starting with the critical role of government incentives and subsidies. In our renewable energy and clean tech operations, these policies are more than tailwinds—they're essential for deploying at scale, lowering levelized cost of energy, and speeding the energy transition. For EcoNova, they've fueled our record backlog of 15.2 gigawatts across solar PV, wind, and battery energy storage systems projects. I'll detail the quantification, regional variations, and how we're strategically positioned.

Quantifying the effect, incentives accounted for about 28% of our adjusted EBITDA this quarter, rising from 22% last year, thanks to heightened monetization of Investment Tax Credits and Production Tax Credits. We captured $347 million in federal ITCs under the Inflation Reduction Act—mainly the 30% base plus 10% domestic content bonus and 10% energy communities adder for our Midwest solar farms. This delivered a 42% effective tax equity yield on the $2.1 billion in project capex during the period. Layer on $112 million from state programs such as California's Self-Generation Incentive Program for our 450 megawatt-hour lithium-iron-phosphate battery projects, and PTCs from our 1.2 gigawatt onshore wind assets at $28 per megawatt-hour, inflation-adjusted. Year-to-date, this has lifted free cash flow by 35%, funding $150 million in share repurchases and progressing our $1.2 billion green hydrogen electrolyzer program.

Trends show a split by region. After the IRA, U.S. clean energy additions reached 32 gigawatts DC in the first half of 2024—equaling all of 2022—boosted by uncapped PTC and ITC transferability, de-risking financing for players like us. Our solar module costs fell 18% year-over-year to $0.24 per watt, aided by IRA manufacturing credits, similar to gains at First Solar and Qcells. Bifacial PERC and TOPCon modules in our 800-megawatt Texas utility projects now hit 22.5% efficiency with 85% capacity factors in high direct normal irradiance zones, tapping the 45X advanced manufacturing PTC at $0.12 per watt for cells and $0.04 for modules.

In the U.S., the IRA's $370 billion clean energy allocation has energized our pipeline—65% of our 25-gigawatt five-year backlog qualifies, including 5 gigawatts of standalone BESS eligible for the full ITC stack following Treasury rules on four-hour systems. We're advancing 2.5 gigawatts DC of tracker-mounted solar with Enphase IQ8 microinverters, grabbing Low Carbon Fuel Standard credits in California at $45 per megawatt-hour for hybrid wind-solar-storage.

Europe's REPowerEU with its €300 billion plan counters U.S. risks from potential 2024 election shifts. Our 1.8-gigawatt offshore wind projects off Denmark, comparable to Orsted's Hornsea, locked Contracts for Difference at €52 per megawatt-hour, plus Dutch SDE++ subsidies of €18 per megawatt-hour for Haliade-X 14-megawatt turbines. This expanded EMEA EBITDA margins by 15%, despite grid bottlenecks. We're pushing 500 megawatts of floating solar PV in the Netherlands, securing €50 million from the EU Innovation Fund for perovskite-silicon tandem cells aiming for 30% efficiency by 2026.

In Asia-Pacific, China's 217-gigawatt solar and wind additions in 2023 lean on feed-in tariffs and VAT rebates, but U.S. tariffs pushed us to IRA-compliant U.S. and Indian manufacturing. Our 1.2-gigawatt Rajasthan solar portfolio gains from India's PLI scheme's ₹24,000 crore incentives, cutting module costs to $0.22 per watt and enabling 25-year PPAs at ₹2.50 per kilowatt-hour. We anticipate APAC delivering 20% of incentive-boosted revenue next year, balancing U.S. policy uncertainties.

We're proactive, investing $75 million in advocacy via the Solar Energy Industries Association and American Clean Power for PTC extensions past 2029 and BESS adders. Our proprietary Incentive Optimization Engine, using AI for cash flow modeling, has freed $620 million in extra tax equity since the IRA, beating peers by 12% on internal rate of return. We project 5-7% EBITDA growth from incentives in fiscal 2024, assuming IRA continuity, with potential from EU Emissions Trading System recycling and Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme for our 800-megawatt Queensland BESS.

Risks persist—U.S. elections might limit ITCs, per Moody's, trimming margins by 300 basis points if transferability ends. We counter with 70% fixed-price PPAs and broad geographies.

Next, a milestone in our commercial pipeline: we secured 1.4 gigawatts of new PPAs, lifting our total backlog to 5.2 gigawatts contracted, ensuring steady cash flows to 2030 and beyond.

We finalized three major deals totaling 1.4 gigawatts in onshore wind, utility-scale solar, and hybrid storage. First, a 750-megawatt onshore wind PPA with a top hyperscaler akin to Google or Microsoft in ERCOT, Texas—a 15-year term with over 45% capacity factor from our next-gen 6-megawatt turbines with 160-meter rotors, aligning with grid renewable mandates. Second, 450 megawatts of fixed-tilt solar-plus-storage hybrids in CAISO, California, to a major utility under PG&E, using our proprietary 700 kilowatt-hour per megawatt four-hour BESS for dispatchable profiles under NEM 3.0, stacking energy arbitrage, ancillary services, and capacity. Third, a standout 200-megawatt offshore wind PPA in the U.S. Northeast BOEM area OCS-A 0521 off Massachusetts with a manufacturing corporate buyer—20 years on 14-megawatt Siemens Gamesa platforms with floating foundations, Jones Act-compliant.

Pricing-wise, the weighted average for these new PPAs is $52 per megawatt-hour levelized and inflation-adjusted—up 8% from $48 last year. This captures value despite easing input costs. Our full backlog averages $49 per megawatt-hour, a 12% premium over SEIA's Q2 2024 solar benchmark of $43 and LBNL's wind index of $40 for Plains states. Without 2.5% annual escalators on 85% of deals, base is $47, aided by IRA PTC extensions and elective pay.

U.S. new volume is 65%, with resilient pricing despite rates—our hedged WACC is 6.2%. ERCOT merchant tails help, but fixed offtakes de-risk 70% of our 2-gigawatt Texas queue. Europe's UK CfD Round 4 for 300 megawatts at £44 per megawatt-hour ($56 equivalent) outperforms amid gas swings; we're eyeing Germany's EEG 2023 for solar repowering with 23% bifacial modules lifting PPAs 15% year-over-year.

These fit our Dispatchable Renewables 2.0, with over 60% hybridized storage to fight curtailment in California and PJM. Corporate PPAs now 40% of pipeline, up from 25% in 2022, tapping RE100 for Scope 2 goals—pricing 10-15% above utilities, speeding permits.

Forward, our 10-gigawatt pipeline targets 65% conversion in 2025 at $50-54 per megawatt-hour, with turbine oversizing to 60%+ factors and AI O&M for 2% yield gains, yielding 15-20% ROIC over 8% capital cost.

Turning to overall performance highlights, we're thrilled with results propelled by dispatchable clean energy demand, IRA tailwinds, and execution on our $18.5 billion pipeline. Revenue of $1.42 billion rose 48% year-over-year, beating guidance by 12%, from $1.1 billion EPC on 2.8 gigawatts DC solar commissions—our best quarter—and $320 million ESS from 1.2 gigawatt-hours deployments. EBITDA margins widened 420 basis points to 20.1% on 15% lower polysilicon and $0.22 per watt modules from LONGi and JinkoSolar.

EPS beat consensus by $0.14 at $0.87, backed by $450 million operating cash flow up 75%, enabling $150 million repurchases and $300 million dividends. Backlog $12.4 billion, 85% PPAs at 18-year terms, 12.8% IRRs.

Operationally, Desert Sunburst 850-megawatt California hybrid with TOPCon and 200-megawatt-hour Tesla storage hit $28 per megawatt-hour LCOE, undercutting gas by 40%, generating $45 million LCFS. Atlantic Horizon 600-megawatt New Jersey offshore with Vestas V236-15.0 MW and 70% U.S. content leads BOEM rounds.

Innovation: VerdantFlow solid-state batteries at RE+ 2024 with 95% efficiency, 12-hour duration, 25% cheaper; $250 million DOE ARPA-E grants. Perovskite-silicon tandems at 32.5% efficiency for 2026 rollout, 30% CAPEX cut.

North America 72% growth on IRA tax equity $1.8 billion YTD; Europe 18% on UK CfD JV with RWE; APAC 10% floating solar in Vietnam.

Our hub-and-spoke model divested $400 million non-core wind for hybrids, ROIC 14.2%. ESG: 4.2 million tons CO2e avoided, 45% women leaders.

Q4 guide: $1.5-1.6 billion revenue, $310-330 million EBITDA; FY2024 52% growth, pipeline to $25 billion.

Finally, our operational metrics. We closed Q3 with 5,850 megawatts operating capacity, up 12% year-over-year from 5,220 megawatts and 4% quarter-over-quarter from 5,620 megawatts, adding 320 megawatts led by 200 megawatts from Atlantic Breeze offshore with GE Haliade-X 12-14 megawatt turbines at over 60% efficiency.

Mix: onshore wind 2,950 megawatts (50%, +8%); offshore 1,420 megawatts (24%, +28%); solar 1,280 megawatts (22%, +5%); BESS 200 megawatts/800 megawatt-hours (4%).

Generation: 14.2 gigawatt-hours, +18% year-over-year from 12.0 and +9% quarter-over-quarter from 13.0, fleet capacity factor 28.5% versus IRENA's 25-27%. Boosted by 7.5 meters per second winds, 99.8% availability.

North America (65% capacity): 9.7 gigawatt-hours, 34% CF; Europe (25%): 3.3 gigawatt-hours, 26% CF; APAC (10%): 1.2 gigawatt-hours, 23% CF.

Pillars: $150 million tech for floating wind and tandems; 85% PPAs $45-55 per megawatt-hour; AI curtailment cuts 40%. FY2024 guide: 6,100 megawatts, 52-55 gigawatt-hours.

Now, I'll pass the call to Mike Thornton to discuss our project development pipeline.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 15.2 gigawatts of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Before that, let me update on construction progress and commercial operation dates, central to our growth as a developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale solar PV, BESS, and hybrids across North America and beyond. Our 15-gigawatt pipeline, up 20% year-over-year, taps IRA adders and hyperscaler demand for 24/7 carbon-free power.

In the U.S., EPC partners like McCarthy and Mortenson advanced amid 35% polysilicon drops to $7.50 per kg. Fixed PPAs at $28 per megawatt-hour beat sub-$20 LCOE with HJT bifacial from First Solar and LONGi.

Southwest: Gemini 690-megawatt DC solar + 380-megawatt-hour Tesla BESS in Nevada at 62% complete—civil done, racking 55%, modules 80% on-site with 600W+ TOPCon at 23.5% efficiency, 28% CF. NV Energy GIA set, gen-tie complete; COD Q4 2024/January 2025, full ITC stack. BESS firms 85% evening peaks.

Horizon 450-megawatt DC expansion 48% complete; substation delays resolved with Siemens, 15 megawatts per day panels; COD Q1 2025, 5% under budget via Nextracker.

Texas ERCOT 1.2-gigawatt DC/1.5-gigawatt-hour BESS Rio Bravo cluster 41%—North at 72%, DC energization, Fluence commissioning August, Sungrow 98% efficiency; pre-COD $15 million ancillaries. CODs: North Q3 2024, others Q2 2025, 12.5% IRR.

Northeast/Midwest: 300-megawatt DC Prairie Wind Illinois coal site 35%—Trina PERC + 150-megawatt-hour BESS; $50 million shared line; COD Q2 2025. Empire State 250-megawatt DC New York 28%, hydro hybrid; COD Q4 2025.

Europe: Spain Puerto Real 200-megawatt PV + 100-megawatt-hour BESS 55% with Acciona, Jinko 22.8%; COD Q1 2025. Australia Darwin 150-megawatt DC + 75-megawatt-hour 22%, monsoon delay; COD H2 2025.

Under construction: 4.5 gigawatts DC/3.2 gigawatt-hours BESS, 72% 2024 CODs mechanically complete. Energized 850 megawatts YTD, +40%, via digital twins cutting variances 18%. Trends: bifacial/HJT yields +10-15%, BESS oversize, grid tech.

Risks: 4-6 month module times, Red Sea +5-10% logistics; mitigated by Qcells 8.4-gigawatt U.S. capacity. CODs: 1.8 gigawatts 2024 (up from 1.2), 3 gigawatts 2025, 25% EBITDA growth.

Next, Lena Novak will update on sustainability.

Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions—avoiding 4.2 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent this quarter alone—improving our energy efficiency through AI optimizations and advanced modules, and promoting responsible resource management across our global assets. We're deeply engaged in community initiatives, from workforce training in energy communities to supporting local biodiversity programs near our wind farms. Our ESG efforts, including 45% women in leadership, not only benefit the planet but also deliver long-term stakeholder value by enhancing project bankability and attracting top talent.

I'll now turn the call back to Jordan for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Lena. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Green Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Mike Thornton:
Thanks for the question, John. Supply chain challenges persist but we've navigated them effectively. Polysilicon prices are down 35% since late 2023 to $7.50 per kg, per BloombergNEF, allowing fixed-price locks. Module lead times have stabilized at 4-6 months, though Red Sea issues could add 5-10% to logistics—we've buffered with U.S. partnerships like Qcells' 8.4-gigawatt capacity and inventory stockpiles. EPC mobilization with McCarthy and Mortenson remains ahead in key projects like Gemini at 62% complete, with only minor slips like Horizon's Q1 2025 COD due to heat, not supply. Digital twin modeling has cut schedule variances by 18%, and we've energized 850 megawatts year-to-date, up 40%. Overall, no major timeline hits, positioning us for 1.8 gigawatts CODs this year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with RenewTech Advisors. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Jordan Hale:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets are key to our geographic diversification, hedging U.S. policy risks while tapping scale. In APAC, India's PLI incentives slashed our Rajasthan solar costs to $0.22 per watt, securing 1.2 gigawatts at strong PPA rates; we see 20% incentive revenue from there next year. Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme supports our 800-megawatt Queensland BESS and Darwin solar-battery at H2 2025 COD. Southeast Asia floating solar hedges tariffs via Vietnam assembly. In Europe, REPowerEU funds Dutch floating solar and Danish offshore at competitive CfDs. Strategy: localize supply with IRA-compliant fabs, hybridize for firm power, and corporate PPAs for RE100. Our 10-gigawatt pipeline targets 65% conversion, with APAC and EMEA growing to 30% of backlog.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with EcoInvest Partners. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Jordan Hale:
Mike, competition is heating up, but our tech and execution edges set us apart. We're ahead with innovations like VerdantFlow solid-state batteries at 95% efficiency and 12-hour duration, plus perovskite tandems at 32.5% lab efficiency for 30% CAPEX cuts by 2026—backed by $250 million DOE grants. Capacity factors beat peers at 28.5% fleet-wide via AI O&M and trackers. IRA optimizations yield 12% IRR premiums, and our Incentive Engine unlocks superior tax equity. Hybrid focus—60% new capacity with storage—addresses curtailment where others lag. Divestitures recycle capital to high-ROIC hubs, pushing enterprise value to $28 billion. Amid LCOE drops per Lazard, we prioritize shovel-ready 15-gigawatt pipeline for superior returns.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of EcoNova Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
